= Isolated Connect JSON Schema validation

This package is based on jsonschema 0.33.0 and is renamed `rtdb-validation-jsonschema`.
`UPSTREAM.json` records the registry archive checksum and the original source-file hashes.
The upstream MIT license and original manifest are retained.

The local dependency chain uses `rtdb-validation-referencing` 0.33.0 and `rtdb-validation-json` 1.0.151.
Only the renamed JSON package enables `arbitrary_precision`.
The workspace's ordinary `serde_json::Value` and its features are independent.
The Connect adapter constructs the isolated value tree directly, preserving user object keys that resemble serde's private numeric marker.
Connect disables HTTP and file reference retrieval and supplies Registry resources explicitly.

The numeric core stores normalized coefficient digits and an arbitrary signed decimal exponent.
Comparison aligns digits without expanding powers of ten.
Divisibility uses modular exponentiation for positive scale differences and coefficient divisibility for negative differences.
Minimum, maximum, exclusive bounds, multipleOf, numeric const/enum equality, uniqueItems hashing and integer classification use this core.
Count bounds saturate above u64 because addressable Rust strings and containers have fewer than u64::MAX elements.
MultipleOf errors retain the original exact JSON number.
The Connect conversion region reserves scratch for both payload and compiled-schema numeric operands before adapting or validating a record.

The copied upstream tests remain available alongside source regressions added to the numeric core and Connect boundary.
No executable verification has been performed during the source-only implementation phase.

Connect selects `with_jvm_registry_semantics` to retain the pinned Confluent 7.8 numeric loader and validator behavior.
The option keeps generic meta-schema validation and adapts only numeric annotations at actual schema nodes for that validation pass.
Original count and multipleOf values remain available to their keyword compilers.
Everit draft4/6/7 uses integral Java node classes for integer types and preserves BigDecimal scale in same-class equality.
Modern json-sKema uses BigDecimal text for integer classification and Java scalar/collection hashes for uniqueItems lookup.
Legacy uniqueness indexes compatible decimal-scale signatures with Roaring posting sets; modern uniqueness uses ordered hash/value keys.
Neither path scans growing native hash-collision buckets.
Count predicates retain signed Java narrowing, including modern contains' distinction between an actual integer zero and a wrapped or decimal zero on empty arrays.
Source regressions cover the five supported drafts and retain existing nonnumeric meta-schema structure checks.

Broader JVM boundaries remain open for isolated UTF16 surrogates, Connect Decimal carriers beyond 64 digits, and nonnumeric schema-loader/format parity.
The numeric compatibility option does not claim those boundaries complete.
